handoff.entry_conditions: Observable entry cue: the fingers are closed, peg_pose is attached to tcp_pose, and the peg has just begun lifting from the box (at index 1120 peg z is about 0.028-0.040 m across demonstrations). The responsibility requires maintaining the grasp, lifting to clearance, rotating the peg from its initial approximately [0.707,0,0,0.707] quaternion toward the hole-axis orientation, and transporting it above the target.
handoff.exit_conditions: By the stop at 1500 the peg remains closed-grasped, is nearly identity-oriented, is at hole height near z 0.099 m and y about 0.177-0.179 m, and has begun motion along +x toward/into the square hole (center x ranges about -0.252 to -0.185 because occurrence timing varies). The outgoing overlap intentionally includes descent and initial insertion rather than ending at a brittle single pre-insert frame.
handoff.failure_signatures: Peg does not remain coupled to the TCP; gripper opens; peg stays below box-wall clearance; orientation fails to converge toward the hole axis; lateral y or z remains far from hole center; or the peg approaches the fixture before alignment. No demonstrated recovery exists for a dropped peg, collision, or a bad grasp.
handoff.overlap_role: Incoming overlap with retrieve_peg_from_box is [1120,1270), 150 actions/7.5 s per trajectory, covering the low closed-grasp state through high clearance and initial turning. Outgoing overlap with align_and_insert_peg is [1380,1500), 120 actions/6.0 s per trajectory, covering final orientation/lateral alignment, descent, and early insertion. The expected benefit is that either neighbor can own the shared transition for several execution chunks.
handoff.successor_readiness: align_and_insert_peg can take over once the grasp is stable and the peg is approximately axis-aligned above the hole. The shared start at 1380 admits some remaining lateral correction (notably demo12205 has peg y about 0.160 m), while later states are centered near y 0.18 m and descend toward z 0.10 m.

name: Lift, turn, and stage peg at hole
segmentation_rationale: This is the long grasp-maintenance and reorientation responsibility, distinct from both acquisition and contact-rich insertion. Across demonstrations the segment starts just after closure with the peg still low, lifts it to roughly 0.43-0.49 m, transports from the box toward positive y/x, and changes peg quaternion toward identity. In demo12200, z reaches 0.428 m at 1240; the peg travels and rotates through 1280-1380; then it is aligned above the hole and descends through 1400-1460. Actions through 1500 are retained as deliberate overlap with insertion. Expected benefit is robust staging under positional variation; successful nominal paths do not establish collision recovery.
